boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Guard Hill record (August 16, 1864) in Sheridan's Valley Campaign [August-October 1864]. The August 11-15 advance to Cedar Creek and the August 17 fight at Winchester are context. Campaign-wide marches, destruction, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions; the live field reads zero. Sheridan says Merritt's division was attacked by Kershaw's division and Wickham's and Lomax's brigades of cavalry, and that only Devin's and Custer's brigades were engaged; his 1866 report puts his whole army's effective line-of-battle strength on August 13 at about 18,000 infantry and 3,500 cavalry. NPS names Kershaw's division and Fitzhugh Lee's cavalry under Anderson. Pond quotes Grant's August 12 estimate that Early with the reinforcement could not exceed 40,000 (read 4.0,000 in OCR), and says the reinforcement proved to be one infantry and one cavalry division.
claims.rationale: Unit identifications, an army-wide figure three days earlier and a secondhand estimate; no count of the forces at the ford. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

Sheridan's 1866 report says he resolved to fall back and carry out his instructions to destroy forage and subsistence, and prints his August 16 order to Torbert to destroy wheat and hay and seize useful mules, horses and cattle.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 550 total; the live field reads 551 (US 71; CS 480). Sheridan's August 17 dispatch gives 2 colors, 24 officers and 276 men captured; his 1866 report 2 flags and 300 prisoners. Pond says nearly 300 prisoners and two flags, with Merritt's loss 60 (read GO in OCR); NPS says about 300 were captured.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Merritt's, Devin's and Custer's reports, Torbert's report, Anderson's and Kershaw's reports and Hotchkiss's journal remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office and field despatches; it quotes Sheridan's, Torbert's, Wright's and Early's reports and despatches and is not independent of them. Sheridan's dispatches of August-September 1864 and his report dated New Orleans, February 3, 1866 are one family of interested Union accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XLIII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
